answer: In an AI agent economy, each participant must lock an ivory stake of verifiable compute capacity linked to a single hardware root. Continuous market activity requires emitting a measurable pulse of signed proofs that neighboring agents cross-check in real time. A determined attacker seeking many sybil identities therefore faces the cost of replicating distinct glacier-scale resource pools rather than cheap virtual clones, quickly exhausting capital while detection thresholds rise with every failed proof.
